findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/expr/reader.go:199 — enableSqlExpressions returns false on every path, rejecting all SQL expressions even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled.
[High/bug] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:17 — RunCommands unconditionally returns “not implemented”; sql.TablesList calls this stub, causing table-reference extraction to fail for every SQL statement.

[High/bug] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — QueryFramesInto replaces the working DuckDB implementation with an unconditional error, causing every SQL command reaching Execute to fail even after the feature gate is corrected.

goldens.comment: The enableSqlExpressions function has flawed logic that always returns false, effectively disabling SQL expressions unconditionally:
The DB methods NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList in pkg/expr/sql/db.go return hardcoded 'not implemented' errors after removing the go-duck dependency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:21 — QueryFramesInto replaces the working DuckDB implementation with an unconditional error, causing every SQL command reaching Execute to fail even after the feature gate is corrected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that pkg/expr/sql/db.go introduces a new DB struct with QueryFramesInto method that always returns 'errors.New("not implemented")'. In pkg/expr/sql_command.go, the Execute method now uses 'db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()' and calls 'db.QueryFramesInto()', which will always fail. However, looking at pkg/expr/reader.go, the enableSqlExpressions function always returns false (due to inverted logic and hardcoded return false), so SQL expressions are effectively disabled. The finding correctly identifies that QueryFramesInto is a stub that will fail, but the feature gate prevents reaching this code. Still, if the feature gate logic were fixed, the stub would cause failures. The finding is technically correct about the stub implementation being broken.
